question: What walking speed is generally used to calculate pedestrian clearance time, and what alternative speed may be used with an extended push-button feature?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The evidence provided is insufficient to answer this question. None of the excerpts state a walking speed value (in feet per second or otherwise) used to calculate pedestrian clearance time, nor an alternative walking speed associated with an extended push-button feature. The excerpts address extended push button press mechanics, signage, audible features, and the relationship between the pedestrian change interval, buffer interval, and calculated pedestrian clearance time — but the actual walking speed figures (which would appear in Paragraphs 7 through 16 of Section 4I.06, referenced but not included here) are not present in the evidence. Citations: - Section 4I.06 Standard §4 (p.724)
gold_answer: The general walking speed is 3.5 feet per second. Up to 4 feet per second may be used to evaluate sufficiency where an extended push-button press provides slower pedestrians a longer clearance time.
